segments.text: Okay, let's get started.
This is our weekly SNAP Assist sync.
The main topic today is the pilot with Riverbend Legal, which starts on December fifteenth.
On the data side, the ingestion pipeline now handles scanned PDFs with OCR.
The open problem is that some contract scans are tilted, and accuracy drops to about eighty percent on those.
That matters, because Riverbend mostly sends scanned contracts.
Aarya, can you add automatic page straightening before OCR?
Yes.
I'll have it done by December fifth.
On the model side, we tested Qwen3 4B against the 1.7B model on our twenty sample contracts.
The 4B model got the right owner and deadline in eighteen of twenty.
The 1.7B model only got thirteen.
So I recommend we ship the 4B model.
Agreed.
Decision: we go with the 4B model for the pilot.
One concern: the 4B model takes about twenty seconds per document on older laptops.
I'd like to add a progress bar and let people keep working while it runs.
Good idea.
Sai, please build the progress bar and background processing before the pilot starts.
Will do.
I'll target December tenth so we have time to test.
I'll also write a short test set of tricky contracts so we can catch mistakes before Riverbend does.
I can finish that this Friday.
Great.
Last item: Riverbend asked for written proof that no data leaves the device.
I'll prepare a one-page privacy summary with our network test results and send it to their IT lead next Monday.
So to recap: Aarya does page straightening by December fifth, Sai does the progress bar by December tenth, Niharika writes the test set by Friday, and I send the privacy summary on Monday.
Thanks, everyone.
